institution_or_company.name: DXOMark camera quality testing, scores and reviews

paper.title: Adapting DeQA-Score for Attribute-Specific Portrait Quality Assessment

details: Studied the performance of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) - DeQA-Score for Image Quality Assessment (IQA) on public (KonIQ, SPAQ, KADID) and internal datasets.
Adapted model outputs to align with DXOMARK’s Just-Objectionable-Difference (JOD) evaluation standards.
Investigated inference strategies (cropped face/eye, prompt variations, distortion sensitivity tests) to optimize quality prediction on the metrics - SRCC, PLCC, MAE.
Designed and developed fine-tuning approaches (regression, vision-only, LoRA) to improve accuracy and capture separate sub-feature quality scores (contrast, texture, and noise).
Published the paper 'Adapting DeQA-Score for Attribute-Specific Portrait Quality Assessment' and received the Best Student Paper award at IS&T Electronic Imaging 2026.
Developed an event-planning multi-agents system using LangGraph, LangChain, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and integrated various LLM APIs.
Applied Chain of Thought (CoT) and Agent-based Prompting techniques via LangGraph to implement workflows that assist event feature suggestions and schedule generation.
Utilized Few-Shot Prompting along with the Vector Database to generate SQL queries based on the user's requests, facilitating users to check events in database through a chatbot interface.
Established a scalable Kubernetes cluster for internal network deployment, streamlining application management.

Enhanced AI model inference efficiency by integrating Triton Server, configuring advanced options like load repository from S3, dynamic batching, concurrent model execution, and load/unload model on the fly.

Refactored Controller Block for scalability, and developed Service Discovery/Management Server to check available services and store metadata information, enabling seamless communication and efficient storage of AI models.
Developed a Face Recognition pipeline with a 10-member scrum team into existing cameras, reducing expenses of buying timekeepers and cutting 70% of employees' waiting time for attendance check-in.
Achieved an 88% recall and 89% precision on internal data by utilizing YOLOv5 with resized frames of 512 and confidence threshold of 0.8 for Face Detection.

Utilized the pre-trained model FaceNet for feature extraction and developed a fully-connected neural network model with Softmax Regression for Face Classification, resulting in a 77% recall and 97.5% precision with probability of 80%.

mentors.name: Prof. Damien Muselet
mentors.title: Assistant Professor in University of Jean Monnet

details: Design a pipeline that leverages the speed of JPEG compression and the perceptual quality of deep learning, achieving higher quality than traditional JPEG and faster performance than fully neural compression methods.
Achieved a compact model with only 10.14M parameters and an end-to-end encode-decode time of just 0.762s.
At 0.6 bpp, the model reached 31.97 PSNR compared to 29.585 for traditional JPEG.

mentors.name: Dr. Thang Nguyen
mentors.title: Senior Research Scientist in FPT Software AI center

details: Developed a novel masking algorithm, leveraging Divide and Merge and Laplacian techniques to enhance patch importance scoring, resulting in improved video compression performance.
Enhanced image reconstruction quality by integrating Stable Diffusion with text prompts generated via BLIP, leading to significant improvements in PSNR and MS SSIM metrics.

Refined research methodologies by evaluating percentile masking vs random masking, demonstrating that random masking improves model robustness while percentile masking is better suited for inference and product deployment.
Prepared, controlled quality, and mined polyp datasets (Kvasir-SEG, CVC-ClinincDB, and ETIS-Larib).

Retrained Transfuse a 'Parallel Reverse Attention Network' model by using Swin Transformer Blocks instead of vision transformers (ViT), improving mDice from 0.733 to 0.77 and mIoU from 0.659 to 0.7 on ETIS dataset.
